claims.text: Adding an element in a specific amount can improve the hardness and strength of an as-cast high-entropy alloy.
The elemental addition can improve hardness and strength without sacrificing useful mechanical performance.
The improvement requires the alloy to be within a specific temperature range.
The improvement requires the added element to be uniformly distributed.
The added element will form a solid solution with the base elements.
Solid-solution formation will change the alloy's lattice parameter.
Solid-solution formation will increase lattice distortion.
Increased lattice distortion will increase alloy hardness.
Increased lattice distortion will increase alloy strength.
Hardness will increase by at least 10% relative to the untreated as-cast baseline.
Strength will increase by at least 10% relative to the untreated as-cast baseline.
A nonuniform distribution of the added element will result in no significant change in hardness or strength.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as using a specific amount of a certain element, but neither is identified and the uncertainty field states that the exact amount is unknown.

Uniform elemental distribution is declared a condition of the hypothesis, while the proposed falsification experiment deliberately uses nonuniform distribution. A null result outside the stated boundary would not falsify the hypothesis under its claimed conditions.
